description: Lead the Claude community in your city. Host meetups and workshops with event funding, API credits, swag, and early access.

detail.summary:
Claude Community Ambassadors build and lead the Claude community in their city, hosting meetups, workshops, and hackathons for local builders. Anthropic funds the events and supplies content kits, swag, and promotion through its own channels, plus monthly API credits to power live demos.

Ambassadors also get pre-release features and Builders Council sessions to bring community feedback to Anthropic's product teams. The program is global, open to any background (no developer title required), and welcomes more than one ambassador per city.

faq.question: Does it cost anything to join?
faq.answer: No. Event sponsorship, API credits, swag, and resources are all provided at no cost.

faq.question: Is the role paid?
faq.answer: There is no direct payment. Benefits are event sponsorship, API credits, networking, swag, and recognition.

faq.question: Do I need to be a professional developer?
faq.answer: No. You need meaningful experience with Claude Code or Claude Cowork and a record of community involvement, not a developer title.

faq.answer: Usually yes, as long as that company's core business doesn't compete with Anthropic. If you're unsure, mention it in your application.

faq.question: How long does membership last?
faq.answer: It's ongoing while you keep hosting events and stay engaged. You can step away and reapply later.

description: Build with Qoder, share your work, host meetups. A year of free Qoder Credits, beta access, event funding, and merch.

detail.summary:
Qoder's Ambassador Program is a community co-creation program for builders who make Qoder, the AI coding platform, a core part of their workflow. It looks for people with real influence among fellow builders who like sharing what they learn, bringing others together, and carrying honest community feedback back to the Qoder team to help shape the product.

The program was recently reimagined and opened a new round of applications with updated review criteria, so former ambassadors need to apply again. Ambassadors get a year of free Qoder Credits (worth the $200/month Ultra plan), priority beta access, event materials and funding, an ambassador badge with a member number, and limited-edition merch. It isn't a paid or employment role, and each round has a limited number of spots.

Priority access to Qoder beta programs and new features before public release
Official event materials and funding for small meetups, themed talks, and build challenges
An exclusive ambassador badge with your member number, plus chances to be featured on official Qoder channels, including interviews
A place in the official ambassador community with a direct line to other ambassadors and the Qoder team, product co-creation, and invitations to exclusive events
Limited-edition Qoder merch and occasional surprise perks
expectations: Use Qoder as a core part of your workflow and share honest takes on its strengths and limitations

Carry community feedback and insights back to the Qoder team
Stay active throughout your term and help keep the community open and authentic
Apply through the 14-question English application form (about 5 to 10 minutes)

faq.question: Who can apply?
faq.answer: Anyone 18 or older who believes in Qoder and likes to create and share: developers, creators, educators, community organizers, or professionals using AI to change how they work.

faq.question: Do I need a big following?
faq.answer: No. Real influence, consistent hands-on work, and the ability to connect with and inspire others count for more than follower numbers.

faq.question: Do I need to be a tech expert?
faq.answer: No. In line with Qoder's "Beyond coding. Create anything." motto, builders from any background are welcome to explore AI-powered creation with their own expertise.

faq.question: How are applications reviewed?
faq.answer: The team looks at your understanding of Qoder, hands-on experience, influence and potential to connect communities, and the value you hope to create. Each round has limited spots, and the Qoder team reaches out to good fits about next steps.

faq.question: I was a Qoder Ambassador before. Do I need to apply again?
faq.answer: Yes. The refreshed program opened a new round with updated review criteria, and returning and first-time applicants both apply. Past participation and contributions are considered in the review.

faq.question: Is this a paid role?
faq.answer: No. It isn't an employment position or a paid endorsement. Ambassadors are supported through product benefits, event support, official recognition, and chances to connect.

description: Host meetups, lead local communities, and create content. Event grants, early product access, and free LangSmith.

detail.summary:
The LangChain Ambassador Program brings together some of the most active members of LangChain's global community. Ambassadors are volunteers who host meetups, lead local or online communities, and create educational content that makes agent engineering with LangChain, LangGraph, and LangSmith easier to pick up.

Ambassadors get early looks at new products, grants to sponsor their events, free LangSmith access, swag, and a direct line to the LangChain team. There's no open application right now: the last public round ran through an Airtable form that closed on September 26, 2025, and that form is no longer public. Community Champions (open-source contributors) and LangChain Experts (forum helpers) are related ways to get involved in the meantime.

faq.question: Can I apply right now?
faq.answer: Not at the moment. LangChain opens ambassador applications in rounds. The last public round ran in September 2025 through an Airtable form that closed on September 26 and is no longer public. Follow LangChain on LinkedIn, X, or Threads to catch the next call.

faq.question: Is this a paid role?
faq.answer: No. Ambassadors are volunteers, supported with event grants, free LangSmith access, swag, and promotion.

faq.question: Who is a good fit?
faq.answer: People who are passionate about agent engineering and already host events, run communities, or create content around LangChain, or are ready to start.

faq.question: Are there other ways to get involved?
faq.answer:
Yes. Community Champions are open-source contributors recognized for fixing bugs, tackling issues, adding features, and writing docs. They get direct access to the team, a say in the roadmap, priority reviews, and swag, and the path starts with contributing to LangChain's open-source packages.

LangChain Experts are volunteers who answer questions and share best practices on the LangChain Forum, in LangChain Academy discussions, and in the community Slack.

description: Host 3+ n8n meetups a year. Event budget, swag, private Slack, and free n8n licenses for educational use.

detail.summary:
n8n ambassadors are community members who host meetups and workshops, share what they know about n8n, and bring local automation builders together. You don't need to be a professional event organizer or a developer: if you've built with n8n for a year or more and enjoy helping others, you're who the program is looking for.

Ambassadors host at least three events a year, represent n8n at tech events in their region, and stay involved for at least 12 months. In return, n8n funds events and sends swag, provides onboarding, playbooks, and a private Slack, and gives complimentary Cloud and Enterprise licenses for educational use, plus a feature on the Meet the ambassadors page and a forum badge.

Bring local builders together and help newcomers feel welcome

Have used n8n for 12 months or more and have some event experience, or be keen to learn

faq.question: Do I need to be a developer or n8n expert?
faq.answer: No. If you've used n8n for 12 months or more and enjoy sharing what you've learned, you qualify.

faq.question: What kinds of events can I host?
faq.answer: Anything from casual coffee meetups to full workshops or hackathons. You choose what works for your local community.

faq.question: What if I'm not sure I can host 3 events a year?
faq.answer: Apply anyway. The n8n team will work with your availability, and you can step down at any time.

faq.question: Is this a paid role?
faq.answer: No. It's a volunteer program, backed by support, resources, and recognition from n8n.

faq.question: Will n8n help me find a venue or speakers?
faq.answer: Yes. Especially for your first event, the team guides you through each step.

faq.question: How does applying work?
faq.answer: Four steps: fill out the application form about you and your city, record a short intro video, have a quick chat to align expectations and sketch your first event, then onboard by joining Slack and getting your welcome kit.

faq.question: Who do I contact with other questions?
faq.answer: Email the team at ambassadors@n8n.io.
